title: Blue Moon

A tour-de-force both interior and mannered by Hawke, for the only director who can bring that kind of performance out of him; Qualley and Scott match him in their paired rejection scenes. Occasional hey-its-that-guy intrusions (“Weegee, take a picture!”) and the weird “height wizardry” involved in depicting 5’10” Hawke as the 4’11” Hart briefly distract, but not fatally.—KH

title: May December
blurb: TV actress Elizabeth (Natalie Portman) arrives in Savannah to research her upcoming role as Gracie (Julianne Moore), who at 36 seduced a 13-year-old and remains married to him (Charles Melton) 20 years later. If Haynes’ influences were Ridley Scott and John McTiernan instead of Douglas Sirk and Joe Losey, he could have called this movie Alien vs Predator, and watching Portman as a soulless chameleon work on (and against) Moore’s damaged sociopath is voyeuristic delight. Haynes shoots the film alternatingly flat and fuzzy, like a somewhat jazzed-up true-crime drama, while playing with a wildly melodramatic score almost from the first beat.—KH

title: No Other Choice
blurb: Desperate to keep his home and family intact, laid-off paper mill manager Man-su (Lee Byung-hun) plans to kill a more successful paper mill manager, along with the superior candidates for the ensuing job vacancy. Son Ye-jin takes on the harder role as Man-su’s increasingly unhappy wife, and her grounded delivery keeps the movie from spinning out of control in Park’s increasingly daring and dissonant shots and Kim Sang-bum and Kim Ho-bin’s drum-snap edits. Gorgeous, innovative, clever, and mordant, a worthy Westlake adaptation for those who claim it can’t be done.—KH
src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: No Other Choice, Hamnet, Jay Kelly · 2026-01-13

title: Nouvelle Vague
blurb: In 1959, frustrated critic Jean-Luc Godard (Guillaume Marbeck) gets his chance to direct his debut film, Breathless. Linklater shoots and cuts this love letter to Godard’s work in completely un-Godardian fashion (although in black-and-white and in French and in a 4:3 aspect ratio), which explains much of why I found myself engrossed in the story and sympathizing with the characters. Much of the rest is Zoey Deutch’s star turn as a frustrated Jean Seberg, who cannot believe she’s stuck doing this movie for this jerk.—KH

O’Connor does his best to put depth on his, but he’s almost the only one given the chance. Like every film in the series, it looks great, though, which is not nothing.—KH

title: Destroying a World That Doesn't Exist
blurb: Avery (Owen Yarnold) tracks the supposed builder, D3rLord3 (Wifies), and we watch D3rLord3 try to seal up the King in Yellow, who he unleashed by exploring the mysterious instance. Two hours plus runtime and explanations for many of the first film’s brilliantly elliptical mysteries lessen the tension and horror in the sequel, although we get far more explicit Yellow Mythos in this one. The Minecraft scenery is if anything even better and more evocative this time around, though.—KH
src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: A Magic Shirt, the Last Mr. Moto Novel, and the Yellow King in Minecraft · 2026-05-05

title: The Empty Man
blurb: Folk-horror mystery: a retired cop hunts a missing teen and uncovers a cult trying to summon an entity from an urban legend.

title: Frankenstein
blurb: Petulant mama’s boy Victor Frankenstein (Oscar Isaac, overacting badly) is hired by weapons magnate Heinrich Harlander (Christoph Waltz, overacting well) to build a living Creature (Jacob Elordi) out of corpses … but who’s the REAL monster, eh? Who? Who? Perhaps the real monster is the filmmaker who gives us 20 minutes of Frankenstein’s daddy issues and no Bride. Del Toro’s patent visual sumptuousness (padded out by some terrible CGI) brings the color his script and characters should have had: Mary Shelley deserves better than this two-dimensional travesty stitched together from her novel and Tumblr.—KH
src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: Del Toro’s Frankenstein, Silver Nitrate, and Ken Finds a New Mystery Writer to Binge · 2025-11-11

title: Fright Night
blurb: Horror-comedy: a teenager becomes convinced his charming new neighbour is a vampire and recruits a washed-up TV horror host to help.

title: Gerald's Game
blurb: Stephen King adaptation: a woman is left handcuffed to a bed in a remote lake house when her husband dies mid-game, and must survive both her predicament and her mind.

title: GonJiam: Haunted Asylum
blurb: Click-hungry college age ghost hunters livestream their illegal exploration of a derelict mental hospital. Familiar premise skillfully executed, for example by cleverly establishing how the characters can be shooting their found footage from every possible angle.—RDL
src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: Play Dirty, Short Spy Stories, Livestreaming Horror, and Meta-Reacher · 2025-10-14

title: Good Boy
blurb: Loyal dog (Indy) senses a sinister force coming for his ill human in the old family house near the woods. Formally brilliant exercise in subjective horror anchored by an endearingly expressive animal actor.—RDL
src: Robin D. Laws: Hong Kong Action, Canine Horror, and Occult Mysteries · 2026-06-02

title: Goodnight Mommy
blurb: Two young boys in Austria wonder if their mother hasn’t been replaced by some other creature when she returns home to recuperate after major reconstructive surgery. It’s easy to see why they fear her so, given that her head is wrapped in bandages that don’t allow for easy recognition. And this film, by Veronika Franz and Severin Fiala, offers up several superbly creepy scares featuring the mummy-ish mommy. But the real story here goes several layers deeper than the suspicion that your parent is no longer your parent. You might guess the twist here before it happens, but in some ways, that’s part of the fun.

title: Heretic
blurb: LDS missionaries, one (Chloe East) bubbly, the other (Sophie Thatcher) reserved, step into the parlor of a hyper-verbal eccentric (Hugh Grant), who has prepared for their arrival with traps both theological and physical. Claustrophobic debate horror in which Grant, playing a character from his current villain phase who thinks he’s as charming as Grant in his leading man days, pounces on every morsel of the script, with East and Thatcher responding in kind.—RDL
src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: Heretic · 2024-12-17

title: History of the Occult
blurb: As a canceled investigative news program ticks down its last broadcast in 1987, its producers (Nadia Lozano, Augustín Recondo, Ivan Ezquerré) desperately try to uncover the piece of evidence that will unlock a black-magic conspiracy at the heart of the Argentine establishment. Superb reality horror justifies the formal experimentation, which veers from retro noir to discontinuous narrative to … —KH
src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: Nosferatu, Wallace & Gromit, and Anglo-Saxon Monsters · 2025-01-07

title: I Know What You Did Last Summer
blurb: Five former high-school besties (Chase Sui Wonders, Madelyn Cline, et al.) negligently cause a fatal car crash and cover it up, but a year later find themselves stalked by a slicker-wearing killer. I remember the 1997 version being somewhat snappier and sharper, but Cline (and returning final girl Jennifer Love Hewitt) provide more depth to their characters than the previous bunch. A soft reboot that doesn’t offer any real surprises, though it annoyingly head-fakes and then soft-pedals the economic stratification that has hit even fictional towns over the last 30 years.—KH
src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: I Know What You Did Last Summer, My Mom Jayne, and the Best Killer Dog Movie to Watch on an Airplane · 2025-07-29

title: I Saw the TV Glow
blurb: In 1996, socially isolated teen Owen (Justice Smith) bonds with slightly older Maddy (Brigette Lundy-Paine) over YA supernatural show The Pink Opaque. Absolutely crippling emotional realism grounds creeping reality horror; special shout-outs to Eric Yue’s cinematography, which looks far better than the budget allows, and the soundtrack of 2020s artists recording imaginary 90s songs.—KH
src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: I Saw the TV Glow, September 5th, The Brutalist · 2025-02-11

title: Late Night With the Devil
blurb: Also-ran talk-show host Jack Delroy (David Dostmalchian) books a victim of demonic possession (Ingrid Torelli) on his show on Halloween night 1977 in a make-or-break ploy for ratings. Beginning with a mockumentary exposition dump, the movie takes off with the “lost master tape” of that suppressed episode and never looks back. Dostmalchian hits the perfect mix of narcissism and flop sweat, and the Cairneses rival Ti West in their 1970s recall. —KH
src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: Killers of the Flower Moon, Chicago Film Fest, and Horror Picks for Halloween · 2023-10-24

title: Men
blurb: Seeking calm after the shocking death of her abusive husband, a woman (Jessie Buckley) books a stay at a gorgeous country house, only to realize that something is very wrong with the local men (all played by Rory Kinnear.) Folk horror of aggressive male insecurity elegantly calibrates its descent from the subtly off-putting to hallucinatory body terror.—RDL
src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: Killers of the Flower Moon, Chicago Film Fest, and Horror Picks for Halloween · 2023-10-24

title: Messiah of Evil
meta: 1974 · Willard Huyck and Gloria Katz · US
blurb: Drawn to the beachside town of Point Dune by her father’s strange behavior, Arletty (Marianna Hill) falls in with occultist-playboy Thom (Michael Greer) and gets menaced by a cult of undead or something. How much of the incoherent, slow-moving action is down to missing scenes and low budgets, and how much is intentionally dream-like atmosphere is probably unknowable. The eerie happenings gain power and authenticity by their very inexplicability and incompleteness, and the movie theater scene is one of the best horror scenes ever filmed , so there you go.—KH
src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: I Know What You Did Last Summer, My Mom Jayne, and the Best Killer Dog Movie to Watch on an Airplane · 2025-07-29

title: A Nightmare on Elm Street
blurb: Slasher landmark introducing Freddy Krueger, who murders teenagers in their dreams.

title: Nosferatu
blurb: Obsessed with fey dreamer Ellen (Lily-Rose Depp), Count Orlok (Bill Skarsgård) lures her husband Thomas (Nicholas Hoult) to Transylvania to convey him to her home of Wisborg. Remake of Murnau’s 1922 Pinnacle enriches it with reference to Stoker’s novel, Browning’s film, and The Exorcist among other influences, while presenting the Gothic world on its own terms as only Eggers can. Robin Carolan’s unnerving score, Jarin Blaschke’s perfectly lit darkness, and the actors’ total commitment are only the high points of the best Nosferatu in a century.—KH
src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: Nosferatu, Wallace & Gromit, and Anglo-Saxon Monsters · 2025-01-07

title: A Quiet Place: Day One
blurb: A despondent cancer patient (Lupita Nyong’o) attempts to survive an invasion of NYC by sound-seeking alien monsters while saddled with an anxious law student (Joseph Quinn.) A rich cinematic text layered with references and resonances, this horror disaster movie stands as the best prequel ever made, taking only what it needs from the franchise it extends.—RDL
src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: A Quiet Place, Day One · 2025-10-21

title: Ready or Not
blurb: Orphan Grace (Samara Weaving) has finally found a family when she marries Alex le Domas (Mark O’Brien), estranged scion of a wealthy games publishing dynasty. As the words “wealthy games publishers” should warn us, they’re in league with Satan, and the resulting bloody game of Hide and Seek provides all the thrills and most of the interest in the film. Watched as a live-action cartoon, it’s fun while it lasts; Weaving isn’t given enough to hang a character on, so that’s all it really can be.—KH
src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: New Tim Powers, The Dirty Dozen with Samurai, and the Quest for Kim · 2025-12-09

title: Searching For a World That Doesn't Exist
blurb: YouTuber Avery (Owen Yarnold) finds a world he didn’t build inside his Minecraft instance, and tries to track down the mysterious builder and crack his enigmatic message. By far the most-watched Yellow King Mythos work is a tight 42-minute reality horror tale taking place inside Minecraft. This does mean lots of watching Avery walk through Minecraft tunnels, but even that can turn chillingly interesting on a dime.—KH
src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: A Magic Shirt, the Last Mr. Moto Novel, and the Yellow King in Minecraft · 2026-05-05

title: Smile
blurb: Therapist Rose Cotter (Sosie Bacon) witnesses a smiling suicide, transferring a demonic entity’s attention to her, attention that manifests in unnatural smiles. This movie suffered from having one of the all-time great trailers , and doesn’t live up to that. Occasional eerie menace, a great high concept, and generally good performances likewise can’t fix a predictable script or really stick the landing. —KH
src: Ken and Robin Recommend: Movies and TV · 2021-11-09

title: The Strangers: Prey at Night
blurb: Slasher sequel: a family staying at a deserted trailer park is hunted by three masked killers.

title: Talk to Me
blurb: Australian horror: teens use an embalmed hand to invite spirits to possess them for a 90-second high, until one of them goes too far.

title: Terrified
blurb: A former pathologist (Norberto Gonzalo), a parapsychologist (Elvira Onetto) and a ghost-breaker (George L. Lewis) team up with a police detective (Maximiliano Ghione) to investigate overlapping haunts in a suburban Buenos Aires neighborhood. Rugna loves to play with perspective, such that no two sightings (or two parts of the same sighting) quite align, adding even more uncertainty to the horror mix. The last act in particular is just unrelenting, perfectly calibrated terror.—KH
src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: Superman, Eddington, Severance, Cloud · 2025-07-22

title: Tribe
blurb: Retired professor Devon Adams (Asma) heads into the Cujamaca Mountains outside San Diego in search of an explanation for his cult-raised best friend’s suicide. Asma cuts big-budget trailers as his day job, which makes this one of the more effective found-footage films even as the editing is so good that it can break suspension of disbelief. The big reveal is appropriately murky, conspiratorial, and apocalyptic, and Asma picks powerful visuals that overlap with the story suggestively without drowning it.—KH
src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: Wednesday, Edgar Allan Poe, and a Murky Found Footage Reveal · 2025-10-07

title: The Visit
blurb: Found-footage horror-comedy: two kids visiting estranged grandparents notice their behaviour growing more disturbing each night.

title: Weapons
blurb: The simultaneous, overnight disappearance of 17 third-graders from a class of 18 sets a number of characters in motion, among them their teacher (Julia Garner) and one kid’s father (Josh Brolin). Over and above Cregger’s assured overlapping-narrative script, his collaboration with cinematographer Larkin Seiple and editor Joe Murphy provide a consummately creepy feel even in seemingly normal moments. Finally, a huge relief to see a horror film that would rather be scary than write an op-ed about trauma .—KH
src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: Weapons · 2025-08-26

title: Who Fears the Devil?
blurb: After the Devil beats his grandpappy (Denver Pyle) in a Defy, young John (Hedges Capers) sets out to defy the Devil’s servants with a silver-stringed guitar. Based on two of Manly Wade Wellman’s Pinnacle John the Balladeer stories, this hippified version still rings somewhat true to the Appalachian rhythms and folkloric horror of the original. The end kind of trails off, but a surprising number of great scenes and effective character moments go a long way; there’s not enough Hoyt Axton music, but there’s more than none. [Also released as The Legend of Hillbilly John.]—KH
src: Ken and Robin Talk About Media: Black Bag, A Noir Mambo Musical, and The John the Balladeer Movie · 2025-03-19

title: The Bank Dick
blurb: A work-shy small-town ne’er-do-well (W.C. Fields) accidentally foils a bank robbery and is rewarded with a job as a bank guard, promptly getting in over his head.

title: Barakah Meets Barakah
blurb: A naive municipal inspector falls for a fiery Instagram star in Jeddah, where any date risks a raid by the religious police. Charming romantic comedy doubles as a sly protest against Saudi social restrictions.

title: The Brothers Bloom
blurb: Two con-artist brothers (Adrien Brody, Mark Ruffalo) draw a lonely, eccentric heiress (Rachel Weisz) into an elaborate, globe-trotting final scheme.

title: Catfight

title: Duck Soup

title: Film with Me in It
blurb: A failing playwright and his actor roommate try to cover up a rapidly mounting pile of accidental deaths inside their cramped Dublin flat.

title: Magic Mike XXL

title: Sons of the Desert
blurb: Stan and Ollie fake illness to sneak off to a fraternal lodge convention in Chicago, then must cover their tracks when their wives learn the truth.

title: Trainwreck
blurb: A commitment-averse magazine writer (Amy Schumer) is unsettled to find herself falling for the sports doctor (Bill Hader) she’s profiling.

src: Outlaw Vern reviews "Christmas Eve in Miller's Point" · 2025-12-30

title: The Christophers

title: Hit Man

src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: Furiosa, Hit Man · 2024-06-25

Co-written by Baumbach and Emily Mortimer, the screenplay’s perfectly sculpted dialogue and scene construction provide the platform for brilliant performances from Clooney, Sandler, Laura Dern, and, in a barn-burner one-and-done, Billy Crudup.—RDL
src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: No Other Choice, Hamnet, Jay Kelly · 2026-01-13

blurb: On a bad day in an Austin Hooters-style restaurant, accumulating crises test the unrewarded competence of beleaguered manager Lisa (Regina Hall.) Observational workplace ensemble drama finds a transcendent nobility in the neverending struggle against everyday bullshit.—RDL
src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: New Neal Stephenson, An Aptly Named Action Movie, and a Classic M. R. James Adaptation · 2024-12-10

title: Coherence
blurb: Over dinner during a comet’s rare pass, eight old friends discover parallel versions of their house and themselves multiplying just outside the door.

title: The Martian

title: Rise of the Planet of the Apes

title: The Signal

title: Under the Skin
blurb: An alien prowls the streets of Scotland in human form (Scarlett Johansson), luring solitary men into an otherworldly void, until encountering something that unsettles her purpose.

title: War of the Worlds
blurb: A divorced dockworker (Tom Cruise) struggles to get his children to safety as towering alien war machines emerge from beneath the earth and lay waste to humanity.

title: Arrival
blurb: A linguist (Amy Adams) is recruited to communicate with newly arrived aliens, and language reshapes her sense of time.

title: Companion
blurb: A shocking incident at a Russian mogul’s secluded manor reveals leads a drippy dude’s (Jack Quaid) devoted girlfriend (Sophie Thatcher) to the awful discovery that she is in fact an android programmed to adore him. Thatcher’s yearning, quicksilver performance goes straight to the horror hall of fame in this ingeniously twisty, comic reversal of robot terror tropes.—RDL
src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: Companion, The Shrouds, Dr. Mabuse · 2025-05-13

title: The Gorge
blurb: Traumatized snipers, one west bloc (Miles Teller), the other east bloc (Anya Taylor-Joy) fall in love from opposite sides of the monster-filled secret canyon they’ve been stationed to guard. The stars turn up all the sizzling charisma a technothriller romance creature feature needs, and then some.—RDL
src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: KPop Demon Hunters, The Gorge, and Anglo-Saxons vs Vikings · 2025-08-12

title: Predator: Badlands
blurb: After his father orders him killed for supposed weakness, a dogged predator (Dimitrius Schuster-Koloamatangi) heads to a planet populated by deadly animals to seek the ultimate trophy, reluctantly teaming with a damaged, unusually chipper Weyland-Yutani android (Elle Fanning.) Rousingly constructed adventure thriller makes clever use of the established crossover between Predator and Alien and showcases Fanning in a gift of a dual role as it hits one great beat after another.—RDL
src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: Wake Up Dead Man, Predator: Badlands, amd the Whole Kill Bill · 2025-12-16

title: Significant Other
blurb: Sci-fi horror: a couple (Maika Monroe, Jake Lacy) backpacking in the Pacific Northwest find their rocky relationship is the least of their problems once a shapeshifting alien arrives.

title: Timecrimes
blurb: Fleeing an attack from a mysterious bandaged figure, an obdurate everyman (Karra Elejalde) jumps into a time machine, which takes him just far enough into the past to unleash a cascade of twisting consequences. Black comic twist on time travel tropes driven by the protagonist’s headlong insistence on the wrongest available decisions.—RDL
src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: Power Fantasy, Sci-Fi Tarot and the Count of Monte Cristo · 2025-02-18

title: The Universal Theory
blurb: At a physics conference in the Austrian Alps in 1962, grad student Johannes (Jan Bülow) meets pianist Karin (Olivia Ross) amid increasingly surreal (and murderous) machinations. If you can imagine a beautifully-shot paranoid SF thriller about the many-worlds interpretation of quantum mechanics (which in our timeline was proposed in 1957), this is one possible outcome of that imagination. —KH
src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: Killers of the Flower Moon, Chicago Film Fest, and Horror Picks for Halloween · 2023-10-24

title: Azumi
blurb: Raised from childhood as an assassin, Azumi (Aya Ueto) is sent out with fellow trainees to kill the warlords threatening to reignite Japan’s civil wars.

title: The Equalizer
blurb: A quiet hardware-store employee (Denzel Washington) with a hidden past as a black-ops operative unleashes lethal skills to protect a young woman from the Russian mob.

title: Headshot
blurb: A bullet lodged in an amnesiac hospital patient’s (Iko Uwais) brain keeps him from remembering he was raised as a super-henchman for a legendary gangster — but his former allies haven’t forgotten.

title: John Wick
blurb: A retired hitman (Keanu Reeves) returns to violence after gangsters kill the dog left to him by his late wife and steal his car.

title: Kilo Two Bravo
blurb: British soldiers become trapped in a minefield near a dam in Helmand Province, and a routine patrol turns into a slow, agonizing rescue effort.

title: Man of Tai Chi
blurb: A gifted tai chi student is lured into an underground fight ring by a wealthy fixer (Keanu Reeves) who broadcasts the bouts to elite gamblers.

title: Okja
blurb: A girl in the Korean mountains fights to save her genetically engineered “super pig” from a multinational corporation hunting it for slaughter.

title: Prince of Persia
blurb: An adopted prince and a princess flee assassins while guarding a dagger that can rewind time itself.

title: RRR
blurb: When the British steal a Gond girl in 1920s India, tribal protector Komaram Bheem (N. T. Rama Rao Jr.) teams up with undercover revolutionary Alluri Sitarama Raju (Ram Charan) to save her.

title: Sabotage
blurb: An elite DEA task force led by a hardened agent (Arnold Schwarzenegger) skims cartel cash from a raid, then is picked off one by one in gruesome retaliation.

title: The Suspect
blurb: A former North Korean special-forces operative, disavowed and hunting his family’s killer, becomes the prime suspect in the murder of a man who trusted him.

title: Why Don't You Play in Hell?
blurb: A ragtag film crew embeds with a yakuza clan to shoot a real gun battle for their movie, colliding with a boss’s daughter cast as the star and a rival gang’s vengeance.

title: 11 Rebels
blurb: Condemned prisoners accept an offer of reprieve to defend a fort long enough for a double-dealing clan to play both sides of the Boshin War. Ensemble cast samurai war film combines classical storytelling with contemporary gore effects.—RDL
src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: New Tim Powers, The Dirty Dozen with Samurai, and the Quest for Kim · 2025-12-09

title: The Beekeeper
blurb: Cyber-scammers provoke the righteous wrath of a retired super-assassin (Jason Statham.) Grounded secondary characters and a tongue-in-cheek sensibility provide the variations in this cleverly assembled addition to the Statham filmography.—RDL
src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: The Beekeeper, Poker Face, and a Poe/Batman Crossover · 2024-04-30

title: The Count of Monte Cristo
meta: 2024 · Matthieu Delaporte and Alexandre de La Patellière · France
blurb: On the verge of marriage above his station to Mercedes de Moncerf (Anaïs Demoustier), sailor Edmond Dantès (Pierre Niney) is betrayed by her jealous cousin and imprisoned in the Chateau d’If black site. Lushly filmed and produced swashbuckler strips down Dumas’ Pinnacle ur-revenge thriller to a mere three hours, staying mostly true to the original while softening some blows for modern audiences.—KH
src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: Power Fantasy, Sci-Fi Tarot and the Count of Monte Cristo · 2025-02-18

title: Freaky Tales
blurb: Four interweaving stories featuring anti-Nazi punks, up and coming rappers, a weary leg-breaker (Pedro Pascal), a corrupt cop (Ben Mendelsohn), and a katana-wielding basketball hero (Jay Ellis) celebrate the spunky underdog culture of 80s Oakland. Genre-hopping hometown valentine nods to the less frequently stolen pages of the Tarantino playbook.—RDL
src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: Bugonia, Freaky Tales, and Junji Ito’s Cat Diary · 2025-11-04

title: Kill Bill: The Whole Bloody Affair
blurb: Gunned down during her wedding rehearsal, former assassin Beatrix Kiddo (Uma Thurman) survives to take revenge on her would-be killers (Vivica A. Fox, Lucy Liu, Michael Madsen, Daryl Hannah), especially her former mentor Bill (David Carradine). Watched as a complete whole, this most visually arresting of Tarantino’s films also builds surprising weight and momentum from a “nothing but the good bits” tribute to martial arts cinema. Thurman’s acting likewise accumulates power at length; only the jackdaw soundtrack suffers a bit at four-and-a-half-plus hours. [Main changes: Deletes the cliffhanger and recap sequences that ended and started the two films, lengthens the “Origin of O-ren Ishii” anime, restores color and adds violence to the House of Blue Leaves segment, adds a post-credits animated “Lost Chapter: Yuki’s Revenge”] —KH
src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: Wake Up Dead Man, Predator: Badlands, amd the Whole Kill Bill · 2025-12-16

title: The Ministry of Ungentlemanly Warfare
blurb: Desperate to break the U-boats’ stranglehold on Britain, M (Cary Elwes) recruits maverick Major March-Philipps (Henry Cavill) and his team to scuttle the Nazi supply ship in neutral Fernando Po. Rousing action film never quite manages to hold or maintain tension (never Ritchie’s strong suit, Wrath of Man notwithstanding) but looks great throughout (Ed Wild shoots in a lively supersaturated 70s palette) and zips along through a two-hour run time.—KH
src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: New Neal Stephenson, An Aptly Named Action Movie, and a Classic M. R. James Adaptation · 2024-12-10

title: Nobody 2
blurb: Government assassin/wage slave Hutch Mansell (Bob Odenkirk) takes his family (Connie Nielsen, et al.) on vacation to his only good childhood memory, a Wisconsin water park, which turns out to be a front for a murderous smuggling ring led by Lendina (Sharon Stone). The first film worked when it did by contrasting its state-of-the-art violence with a relatively mundane life background embodied by Odenkirk’s schlub character. This one deliberately plunges into a cartoon world almost from the jump, stepping on its few good setups, and even Tjahjanto’s gore-loving camera can’t force much more than the occasional chuckle.—KH
src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: New Tim Powers, The Dirty Dozen with Samurai, and the Quest for Kim · 2025-12-09

title: Prey
blurb: In 1719 Wyoming, young Comanche woman Naru (Amber Midthunder) attempts the ceremonial hunt of an unknown invisible monster. This installment of the Predator series (for indeed it is he) works so well and so naturally not just because of the great monster-hunting set-pieces but because the natural, vivid character building of Naru and her brother (Dakota Beavers) also build the reality of the frontier world the Predator irrupts into. Easily the second-best of the series. –KH
src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: The Sandman, Prey, and a Rock Journalism Icon · 2022-08-16

title: Scare Out
blurb: Counterintelligence squad leader (Yilong Zhu) and his loyal second in command (Jackson Yee) become the prime suspects in a mole hunt. It goes without saying to any serious student of the spy genre that a technothriller melodrama with American adversaries from the grandmaster of mainland Chinese film is required viewing.—RDL
src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: An Under-Celebrated Horror Writer and New Films by Yuen Woo-Ping and Zhang Yimou · 2026-02-24

title: Only Lovers Left Alive
blurb: Centuries-old vampire lovers (Tom Hiddleston, Tilda Swinton), long separated across continents, reunite in Detroit as despair over humanity deepens.

title: The Gilded Lily
blurb: When the charming stenographer (Claudette Colbert) he loves falls for an incognito English lord (Ray Milland) a cynical reporter (Fred MacMurray) turns her into a tabloid sensation. Smart romcom tackles such classic 30s themes as reality stardom and the friend zone.—RDL
src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: Thunderbolts*, Final Destination, Daredevil · 2025-05-20

title: Goodbye Again
blurb: To the consternation of his attentive secretary/lover (Joan Blondell), an easily swayed romance novelist (Warren William) fails to resist the advances of a now-married old flame (Genevieve Tobin.) Witty, lightning-paced stage adaptation squeaks in at the end of the pre-Code era with a depiction of jealousy wreaking havoc on an open relationship. Stalwart comic character actor Hugh Herbert steals the movie as the romantic rival’s affably unconcerned husband.—RDL

title: Materialists
blurb: A New York matchmaker is caught between a wealthy ideal match and a broke ex; a romance set pointedly in the smartphone era. One of Andrew’s 2025 favourites.

title: Bone Tomahawk
blurb: A frontier sheriff (Kurt Russell) leads a small posse across hostile territory to rescue townspeople abducted by a cave-dwelling tribe of cannibals.
src: Ken and Robin / Robin D. Laws

title: The Good, the Bad and the Ugly
blurb: Three gunslingers (Clint Eastwood, Lee Van Cleef, Eli Wallach) chase a fortune in buried Confederate gold across a Civil War-ravaged frontier.

title: Goyokin
blurb: Haunted by a massacre he failed to stop, a wandering samurai (Tatsuya Nakadai) returns to confront his former clan’s plot to repeat the slaughter.

title: Guilty Men
blurb: When a political deal forces the demobilization of local paramilitaries, farmers stuck delivering extortion money to one holdout group are left holding a dangerous bag.

title: The Man Who Shot Liberty Valance
blurb: A senator (James Stewart) recounts, in flashback, how he and a rancher (John Wayne) once faced down a sadistic outlaw (Lee Marvin) terrorizing a frontier town.

title: Open Range
blurb: Free-range cattlemen (Robert Duvall, Kevin Costner) clash with a tyrannical rancher and corrupt marshal after a confrontation in a small Western town turns deadly.

title: The Searchers
blurb: A Civil War veteran (John Wayne) spends years hunting for his niece, abducted by Comanche raiders, as vengeance curdles into obsession.

title: Stagecoach
blurb: Strangers thrown together aboard a stagecoach through Apache territory — among them an outlaw (John Wayne) and a disgraced woman — find their fates and characters tested.

title: True Grit
blurb: A headstrong teenager (Hailee Steinfeld) hires a dissolute U.S. Marshal (Jeff Bridges) and a vain Texas Ranger (Matt Damon) to track her father’s killer through Indian Territory.

title: The Wild Bunch
blurb: An aging gang of outlaws (William Holden), pursued by a former partner turned bounty hunter, plots one last score along the Texas-Mexico border as the Old West closes in.

title: The Harder They Fall
blurb: When the vicious outlaw (Idris Elba) who murdered his parents and scarred him for life is released from prison, gunslinger Nat Love (Jonathan Majors) teams up with Marshal Bass Reeves (Delroy Lindo) to take him down. References the stylistic gestures of the spaghetti western and the studio western’s tradition of treating historical figures as mythic beings capable of fitting any storyline as it escalates from a series of duels for interpersonal dominance into a thrilling shootout finale.—RDL

title: The Act of Killing
blurb: Indonesian death-squad leaders are invited to reenact their 1965–66 mass killings in the film genres of their choosing, staging musicals and gangster scenes.

title: Beware the Slenderman

title: Forbidden Quest
blurb: Framed as a rediscovered 1941 documentary, an old sailor recounts a doomed 1905 Antarctic expedition through archival silent-film footage.

title: The Look of Silence
blurb: An optometrist confronts the men who murdered his brother during Indonesia’s 1965 anti-communist purge, testing their eyesight as he questions them.

title: The Overnighters
blurb: A North Dakota pastor opens his church to desperate oil-boom job seekers sleeping in their cars, straining his congregation and his own family.

title: Secret Trial 5
blurb: Four Muslim men, held for years under Canada’s security-certificate law without charge or access to the evidence against them, recount lives suspended by secret proceedings.

title: Alien Island
blurb: Documentary begins with Chilean shortwave operators’ contacts with UFO witnesses in 1984, which led to lengthy radio discussions with “Ariel,” the representative of an unspecified island in southern Chile called “Friendship.” Without giving away the left turns the story takes, I can say the film makers probably found the hoaxer behind Ariel, and have a good reason for the seemingly irrelevant footage of Pinochet at the beginning. If there’s such a thing as a noir UFO documentary, this is kind of that. —KH
src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: Killers of the Flower Moon, Chicago Film Fest, and Horror Picks for Halloween · 2023-10-24

title: The Perfect Neighbor
blurb: Bodycam footage reveals months of incidents in which a pathologically territorial Florida woman calls police to complain that neighborhood children are playing on an adjacent property, culminating in her fatally shooting one of their mothers. A masterful formal achievement in documentary construction examines American fear culture while honoring the community devastated by its impact.—RDL
src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: The Perfect Neighbor · 2026-03-31

title: Andor Season 2

title: The Muppet Show

title: Only Murders in the Building Season 1
meta: 2021 · Hulu/Disney+, Steve Martin & John Hoffman · US

src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: The Beekeeper, Poker Face, and a Poe/Batman Crossover · 2024-04-30

title: The Sandman Season 1
meta: 2022 · Netflix, Neil Gaiman, David S. Goyer & Allan Heinberg · US

src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: May December, French UFOs, Yokai, and Modern Yoga’s Eliptony Layer · 2024-03-05

title: Arnold J. Haiman’s Nero Wolfe pastiches
blurb: Five fan-written Wolfe stories (Murder at the Gazette; Death of a Doctor; Wolfe at the Door; Major Goodwin Returns; The Return of Major Goodwin), free to download.

title: Auguste Lupa novels (John Lescroart)
blurb: Two mysteries — “Son of Holmes” and “Rasputin’s Revenge” — whose detective Auguste Lupa is strongly hinted to be a young Nero Wolfe.

title: The Body of a Girl
blurb: Newly promoted to Chief Inspector and stationed in the remote suburb of Stoneferry, Bill Mercer investigates a dead body found in a drift island in the Thames. Combines police procedural with a touch of “man vs. town” thriller to superb effect; the Gilbert dry humor here runs a little blacker than his usual. Mercer also stars in a very tight three-novelette series in The Man Who Hated Banks and Other Stories, also Recommended.—KH
src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: Wake Up Dead Man, Predator: Badlands, amd the Whole Kill Bill · 2025-12-16

title: The Calder & Behrens Stories
blurb: Calder and Behrens, both middle-aged British WWII veterans, do “distasteful” jobs for a special counterintelligence committee using a combination of fussy brio and unfussy brutality. Perhaps the hardest genre in short fiction to pull off is the espionage short, and Gilbert succeeds virtually every time at bat. Only when read in rapid succession do the stories seem even slightly formulaic, but good luck reading one short and not immediately inhaling both volumes.—KH
src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: Play Dirty, Short Spy Stories, Livestreaming Horror, and Meta-Reacher · 2025-10-14

title: Death in Captivity
blurb: One of the most original premises for a “locked room” mystery ever: in an Italian POW camp in 1943, a possible informer turns up dead in an escape tunnel that takes four men to open. Gilbert (who actually spent time as a POW in Italy) interweaves a fair-play murder mystery with a classic prison-camp story complete with heroic escape plans, all of it complicated by the fact that the Italian authorities have their own schemes to which the detective is not privy, and their own POW to frame for the crime.—KH
src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: Del Toro’s Frankenstein, Silver Nitrate, and Ken Finds a New Mystery Writer to Binge · 2025-11-11

title: Every Henry Gamadge Novel
blurb: Henry Gamadge, upper-class document authenticator and sometime bibliophile, solves mysteries embedded in family dynamics: an American version of the “country house” mystery genre. Daly was Agatha Christie’s favorite American writer, and her puzzles equal Dame Agatha’s while her characters remain human and three-dimensional. Gamadge’s real superpower is general genteel niceness: he knows everybody and gets along with most people, he’s the only Golden Age detective you’d actually want to hang with. Daly’s New York is the uptown version of Nero Wolfe’s, and her puzzles are better. Start with my most Recommended titles of the sixteen: Arrow Pointing Nowhere, The Book of the Dead, And Dangerous to Know ; then hit the slightly out-of-mode Evidence of Things Seen. –KH

title: Every Patrick Petrella Story
blurb: Gilbert’s longest-running serial character (two novels and 54 shorter stories), Petrella is a half-Spanish, poetry-reading London police detective. Not quite maverick cop, not quite cerebral detective, not quite procedural protagonist, Petrella gives his adventures a specific and hard-to-isolate flavor that not even Gilbert’s other police stories can match. Start where Gilbert started, with the puzzle-inside-a-procedural Blood and Judgement, and then sample the shorter Petrella in Petrella at Q. —KH
src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: Marty Supreme, Roofman, and the Patrick Petrella Stories · 2026-01-06

title: Garrett, P.I. series (Glen Cook)
blurb: Fantasy-noir series whose lead pair — the housebound “Dead Man” and legman Garrett — are, by the author’s own admission, modelled on Wolfe and Archie.

title: A Haunting on the Hill
blurb: Playwright Holly Sherwin rents the empty Hill House with her cast and tech designer to workshop her new witch-trial play, adapted from a Jacobean original, in this (estate-approved) sequel to Shirley Jackson’s Pinnacle novel . Hand was never going to equal the greatest horror novel of all time, so she writes a different story about human frailty colliding with the unnatural, rich in metafiction, drama, and “I just can’t read this next part” dread. It’s not a remake or even a cover version, and it’s barely even a sequel, but it’s another deeply satisfying (and horripilating) Elizabeth Hand novel. —KH

title: The Horror of Abbot’s Grange
blurb: A collection of (mostly) ghost stories misleadingly marketed as “in the M.R. James tradition.” Cowles, a folklorist rather than an antiquarian by tendency, provides blunt and often physical horrors in tales with simple structure and language. The best of them, “The House on the Marsh,” “One Side Only,” and “The Bell,” are quite effective shorts; others provide good scares somewhat vitiated by explanations or exorcisms. The Benedictine Father Placid delivers some of both, in several tales; he’s an under-rated ghost-breaking occult detective.—KH
src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: Slow Horses, Blitz, and a Benedictine Occult Investigator · 2025-05-06

title: Julius Katz & Archie (Dave Zeltserman)
blurb: Award-winning modern Nero Wolfe homage: a reclusive Boston PI and his wisecracking assistant — here an AI — echo Wolfe and Archie. Began in Ellery Queen Mystery Magazine.

title: Lobo Blacke / Quinn Booker series (William DeAndrea)
blurb: Western mysteries pairing a wheelchair-bound ex-lawman with a dime-novelist sidekick — a Wolfe-and-Archie dynamic transplanted to the frontier.

title: Lord Darcy series (Randall Garrett)
blurb: Alternate-history mysteries in a world where magic works; investigator Lord Darcy and his forensic sorcerer Master Sean solve crimes by the rules of fair-play detection.

title: Mack Reynolds — Ultra-Welfare State stories
blurb: SF stories in Analog featuring unnamed but unmistakable Wolfe-and-company characters in a future where the welfare state has abolished crime — and detective work.

title: The Maestro Nostradamus Trilogy
blurb: Three mystery novels featuring the alchemist, astrologer, seer, etc. Nostradamus (the nephew) and his apprentice Alfeo in a 1590s Venice where magic works. Engaging pastiche of Nero Wolfe offers moderately compelling mysteries and rich setting and occult detail. Definitely inspirational for Swords of the Serpentine players. –KH
src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: Banshees of Inisherin, The Maestro Nostradamus Trilogy, and a Hollywood Double Agent · 2023-01-31

title: Mischief
blurb: Out of town hotel guests readying themselves for a prestigious banquet leave their 9 year old daughter with the wrong last-minute babysitter. Tense psychological thriller makes masterful use of incisively drawn multiple perspectives.—RDL
src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: I Saw the TV Glow, September 5th, The Brutalist · 2025-02-11

title: Nine Times Nine
blurb: Writer Matt Duncan has just landed the job of assistant to anti-fraud crusader Wolfe Harrigan when Harrigan is shot in a locked room by a man in the yellow robe of LA cult leader Ahasver—who admits that his astral double committed the murder. Boucher tries to out-impossible John Dickson Carr, including a bravura sequence in which LAPD detective Terence Marshall goes through Carr’s classic “Locked Room Lecture” to try and solve the case; the actual solution falls to Sister Ursula, a nun friend of the Harrigan family. The LA occult scene also gets a lively portrait in this terrific mystery.—KH
src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: Fantastic Four, Weapons, Nobody 2 · 2025-08-19

title: Paint, Gold, and Blood
blurb: The impecunious schoolboy Peter Dolamore stumbles over an art theft, and with his chum Stewart Ives eventually investigates. I am a sucker for all three of the strands of this novel: “boys’ adventure” school story, Hitchcockian “wrong man” thriller, and art theft, and by now I’m less surprised (though no less impressed) when Gilbert eventually but seamlessly weaves three seemingly random separate types of novel into one. As is common with Gilbert, the last quarter of the book clicks up into superb suspense.—KH
src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: Nouvelle Vague, an Obscure New Wave Gem, and The Brain Stealers · 2025-11-25

title: Right You Are, Mr. Moto
blurb: American spy Jack Rhyce is sent to Japan to uncover a Communist assassination plot and the elusive “Big Ben,” but complications arise in the form of last-minute spy partner Ruth Bogart and mysterious manipulator Mr. Moto. The only postwar Mr. Moto novel combines genuinely thrilling espionage minutiae and Marquand’s habitual command of the travelogue with reveals that of course “Moto” is an alias, and of course Mr. Moto’s cartoonish English is a cover.—KH
src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: A Magic Shirt, the Last Mr. Moto Novel, and the Yellow King in Minecraft · 2026-05-05

blurb: When Major MacMorris is blown up with his house, Mrs. Artside has lost a tenor for her church choir but gains a mystery to unravel. Gilbert has fun with the “cozy village” mystery in this one, distributing the investigations between Mrs. Artside, her ex-commando son Tim, and eventually Inspector Hazlerigg. Not especially difficult as a whodunit, a bit of a howdunit, but mostly a chance to follow Gilbert through his felicity with small dramas.—KH
src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: Fantastic 4, The Ax, and a Cozy House Explosion · 2025-12-02

title: Slow Burn (G.M. Ford)

title: Smallbone Deceased
blurb: An annoying trustee turns up dead in a deed box, throwing the august London firm of solicitors into a tizzy, since their senior partner (also deceased) is the prime suspect. Inspector Hazelrigg (and a new hire who can’t have done it) investigate this beautifully constructed classic mystery. Like Sayers’ Murder Must Advertise, the office byplay and incisive characterization carry a whole extra novel with them, allowing Gilbert to enliven the story with dry wit aplenty.—KH
src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: Del Toro’s Frankenstein, Silver Nitrate, and Ken Finds a New Mystery Writer to Binge · 2025-11-11

title: There Is No Antimemetics Division
blurb: Marion Wheeler, the head of the SCP Foundation’s Antimemetics Division, battles an antimemetic world-killer in a series of layered, interrelated short narratives. Mandatory reading for Madness Dossier GMs. —KH

title: Three Bullets (Alan Vanneman)
blurb: A free trio of Nero Wolfe pastiche stories — “Politics Is Murder,” “Invitation to a Shooting Party,” and “Fame Will Tell.”

title: Tremor of Intent
blurb: Adventurous British agent spectacularly bungles his assignment to retrieve an erstwhile school chum, a scientist who has defected to the Soviet Union. Brings unexpectedly deep characterization and Catholic eschatology to an outrageous, stinging satire of Fleming, Greene, and le Carré.—RDL
src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: Late Night With the Devil, Burgess Does Bond, and Oliver Sacks · 2024-07-09

title: Peter Cannon: Thunderbolt
blurb: Peter Cannon, heir to the Ancient Scrolls of a lost civilization, reluctantly defends his Earth against a faked alien invasion. I could write an essay about this intelligent, honest response/homage to Watchmen, but suffice it to say that Gillen’s engagement with the form and the content of comics’ eternal, nigh-fatal masterpiece provides the best possible argument for broad reading in the classics as a basis for creative effort. Its biggest flaw is that unlike its model it doesn’t quite encompass a superhero story -- but Gillen intends that lacuna, as well. Wijngaard’s art counterpoints both Gillen and Gibbons' genius (two difficult tasks!) with remarkable fluidity and strength, and Mary Safro’s coloring quietly amazes. --KH

title: Peter Cannon: Thunderbolt Omnibus
meta: 2015 · Alex Ross & Steve Darnall and Jonathan Lau · Dynamite
blurb: Peter Cannon’s impulsive creation of a dragon tulpa to discourage nuclear testing blows back on every part of his life as old foes and new gather to destroy him. If Gillen & Wijngaard’s take on the same material was near-Pinnacle Recommended, this is near-Recommended Good: the comic never bored me and once or twice genuinely surprised me, but didn’t leave a whole lot behind. It’s funny how Moore’s deconstruction of Cannon has somehow become the template for every major treatment of the character since -- in that respect Ross & Darnall break new (if less inviting) ground by depicting a genuinely confused Thunderbolt rather than an arch Ozymandias. --KH

title: Power Fantasy Vol. 1: The Superpowers
blurb: Beginning with the Trinity detonation, people started getting powers. Six of them have the power to destroy the planet. None of those six really get along. Gillen’s ongoing wrangling with what Watchmen did to the art form has produced a compelling comic that takes some big swings in terms of narrative consequences and risks to audience sympathy; Wijngaard’s art provides clarity of narrative with valuable emotional color contrast.—KH

blurb: A shoe-company executive (Toshiro Mifune) mortgaging everything for a boardroom takeover is told his son has been kidnapped — then that the kidnappers took his chauffeur’s son by mistake, and want the ransom anyway. title: The Train
blurb: Railway inspector and Resistance cell leader Paul La Biche (Burt Lancaster) is forced to prevent Col. Waldheim (Paul Scofield) from stealing a train load of modern artworks from soon-to-be-liberated Paris. Superb acting from the leads down, combined with insanely complex tracking shots, glorious practical effects, and riveting tension, should put this a close second on Frankenheimer’s resume. Instead, film consensus has bizarrely neglected this sublime blend of heist and war film (one I guarantee Christopher Nolan has watched) that wields a powerful philosophical punch.—KH
src: Robin D. Laws: Coyote vs. Acme, The Train, A Useful Ghost · 2026-09-01

title: Coyote vs. Acme
blurb: After a lifetime of pain and suffering from dysfunctional Acme Corp. products, Wile E. Coyote (playing himself) sees small-time legal huckster Kevin Avery’s (Will Forte) ad and decides to sue the megacorp. Although it can’t quite make up its mind (Stakhanovite paean to work itself? anti-corporate fable? the real verdict is friendship?) this lack of focus doesn’t really derail what is essentially an excuse to stitch hilarious Looney Tunes bits (both new and recycled) together. John Cena excels as the Acme corporate counsel, not just in his bullying metier but his craven-ness toward his boss Foghorn Leghorn.—KH
src: Robin D. Laws: Coyote vs. Acme, The Train, A Useful Ghost · 2026-09-01

src: Ken and Robin Consume Media: The Ipcress File, Appointment with Death, and There Are No Fakes · 2026-07-21

title: Appointment With Death
blurb: When tyrannical Mrs. Boynton dies on an excursion to Petra, the authorities call in Hercule Poirot to find the killer. The rare Poirot to actually turn on human motives, we still go through the standard timetable-establishing so dear to Christie’s heart to get there. But the psychology of the Boynton ensemble remains interesting even with the all-knowing 1930s Freudspeak, and without the somewhat-contrived solution, so Good for you, Dame A.—KH

title: Sirât
blurb: A desperate man (Sergi Lopez) seeking his missing daughter seeks her, with preteen son in tow, at a rave held near the North African desert. Beautiful and disturbing, palpably physical fable about first world assumptions of safety and the precarity they conceal.—RDL
src: Robin D. Laws: RVIFF 2026 Capsule Review Roundup

title: Buffet Infinity
blurb: Clips from local TV commercials tell of the growing rivalry between strip mall restaurants and the cosmic hunger for human minds emanating from a nearby sinkhole. Weird, hilarious horror comedy keeps wringing new escalations from its tightly restricted format.—RDL / Second review, Ken and Robin Consume Media 13 October 2026: VHS recordings of UHF-network newscasts and ads tell the story of a cosmic horror invading a city in Alberta. Teetering mix of horror and comedy keeps the plates spinning through a slightly overlong run time (the middle act lags a bit), only once violating its own cinematic rules but with a bit so perfect I can’t really complain. Absolutely one of the most original and effective horror films in an excellent year for horror films.—KH

title: The Old Woman With the Knife
blurb: Aging legend (Lee Hye-yeong) of a vigilante assassin agency realizes a sadistic new punk recruit (Kim Sung-cheol) has her in his sights. Grippingly crafted hit man actioner offers an unexpected relationship between protagonist and antagonist.—RDL
src: Robin D. Laws: RVIFF 2026 Capsule Review Roundup

title: Maldoror
blurb: Dogged young cop (Anthony Bajon) risks career and family in pursuit of a criminal (Sergi Lopez) at the heart of a murderous, well-connected abduction and pedophilia ring. Tense fictionalization of the horrifying Marc Dutroux case stokes fury against engrained Belgian official incompetence and corruption.—RDL

title: Redux Redux
blurb: Against her better judgment, a hardbitten woman (Michaela McManus) who travels to alternate dimensions killing every iteration of the man who murdered her daughter acquires a runaway teen sidekick (Stella Marcus). Superbly realized indie actioner keeps finding new ways to build on its high concept premise.—RDL

title: Obex
blurb: In the pixelly dawning of the digital age, an agoraphobic professional ASCII artist enters a strange video game to rescue his dog from its resident demon. B&W microbudget horror fantasy zigzags between disturbing and silly in its tribute to the healing power of genre nonsense.—RDL

title: Rose of Nevada
blurb: Skint family man signs on to crew a mysteriously returned fishing vessel and along with a rootless fellow recruit is cast back to 1993 in the identities of missing men. Hypnotic weird tale with a bold sound and visual scheme as chronologically displaced as its characters.—RDL
src: Robin D. Laws: RVIFF 2026 Capsule Review Roundup

title: LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight
blurb: Action-adventure across an open-world Gotham with seven playable characters, drawing on Batman across films, comics and television, with combat taking heavy inspiration from the Arkham games. Released 22 May 2026 on PS5, Windows and Xbox Series X/S; 18 September 2026 on Switch 2.

title: Resident Evil
blurb: On the night of the Umbrella outbreak, a medical courier (Austin Abrams) drives a delivery through the snow towards Raccoon City General, hits a woman on a mountain road, and — decently, disastrously — belts her into his passenger seat to get her to help. Cregger’s reboot escalates from zombies into tentacles and worse while holding what Vern calls a perfect Evil Dead II tone: constant laughs from the hero’s ordinary incompetence, none of them at the horror’s expense. Vern rates it the best of the Resident Evil films.

title: Barbarian
blurb: A woman arrives at a Detroit rental to find it double-booked by a stranger, and the house turns out to be the least of it. Cregger’s first feature, and the one that established the handbrake-turn structure he has used since.
src: Seen and enjoyed — Andrew’s own record, added 30 September 2026

title: Ithaqua
blurb: Midwinter hunger haunting Canadian Fort William threatens American mercenary Cole Franklin (Luke Hemsworth) and his Ojibwa bride Ahnung (Leenah Robinson) in ways beyond the nutritional. The new Hammer Films returns to gory period horror with this fine wendigo movie that barely hints at cosmicism but manages the threat of starving in the snow very well, not least thanks to cinematographer Bryn McCashin and some good practical FX.—KH

title: Lanterns — Season 1
blurb: The past reveals its secrets when self-contained former Green Lantern trainee John Stewart (Aaron Pierre) returns to a small Nebraska town to investigate the murder of rumpled mentor and rival Hal Jordan (Kyle Chandler). Moody crime drama with a puzzle-piece chronology both downplays and honors its four-color origins.—RDL

title: Predators
blurb: Documentary examines the pedophile-hunting efforts of Chris Hansen’s To Catch a Predator segments on Dateline NBC, his current streaming venture, and his amateur YouTube imitators. Shows how hard the adult decoys work to seduce their targets into sex crimes, and how readily people can rationalize cruelty when the target is probably an abuser and they’re making a buck on it.—RDL

title: Hope
blurb: Na Hong-jin's first film since The Wailing: a sprawling 156-minute monster/alien action picture set in the rural town of Hope Harbor. Police chief Ko Bum-seok (Hwang Jung-min), his cousin Sung-ki (Zo In-sung) and a rookie officer played by Hoyeon — who Vern says steals the film — face creatures performed in motion capture by Michael Fassbender, Alicia Vikander, Taylor Russell and Cameron Britton. Vern points to Tremors, Jaws and Mad Max, finds it funny and sometimes mean, likens the effects to Harryhausen, and calls it something special, though he expects the ending to divide people. NEON is distributing in the US.
